_comment: Adaptive-result registry (ADR-035): every check that may legitimately record ADAPTED. An ADAPTED verdict without an entry fails the run; a registered entry that starts passing fails (escalate) until promoted. `versions` pins observed harness versions; `*` covers any (bootstrap state — pin after the first probed runs). Update `observed_at` on any touch.

adaptive.reason: Antigravity CLI offers no documented explicit-only invocation mechanism, so the user-only skill stays visible to the model; recorded as a vendor limitation, never fabricated.

Antigravity executes `hooks.json` hooks only when signed in, and the vertical now runs signed in: `hooks-vendor-hook-executes` passes there, with a vendor-format deny hook at ~/.gemini/config/hooks.json denying run_command in the same session. What is still unobservable is UZE's own delivery: the harness reads no hooks.json from a plugin directory. `agy plugin validate` counts the generated plugin's three hooks, the plugin is listed with a `hooks` component and enabled in config.json, and the session still reports `loaded 0 named hooks from 0 hooks.json file(s)` — it never opens the file. The vendor's own shipped plugin guide documents the opposite ("Hooks defined in `plugins/<name>/hooks.json` are registered and run during the agent's lifecycle"). Measured live each run by `hooks-delivered-hooks-loaded`.

The same vendor-format control hook that fires in the vertical's signed-in session runs nothing under GEMINI_API_KEY: the harness loads it (hooks_manager: loaded 1 named hooks) and the command reaches the permission prompt instead. The executor reads `enable_json_hooks`, field 17 of `exa.cortex_pb.CustomizationConfig`, which arrives only over the CloudCode `v1internal` backend the signed-in CLI speaks; serving `json-hooks-enabled` alone does not open the gate. Vendor bug google-antigravity/antigravity-cli#893 (open 2026-08-28); #78 records that Google does not support the Gemini API-key path at all. The declaration fails the day the hook fires under an API key.

See that entry for the measurement.

OpenCode V2 beta: the real runtime answers a scripted call to the delivered tool name with `Unknown tool` — the tool message exists but the MCP server never ran.

OpenCode V2 exposes no input-based block (spec: the action-level deny lives in the permission hook, which carries no tool input); the guard handler runs via the owned bridge and the tool still executes.
OpenCode V2 exposes no input-based block, so a first-deny cannot stop later handlers observably; both handlers run and neither marker reaches the conversation.
The delivered MCP tool is not exposed on this channel, so handler execution through the bridge is not observable — the turn and marker semantics are the real harness evidence.
